title: WISE band energy requires emission outside a passive planetary lobe in G4466 if the emission is isotropic
abstract: We test the energy budget of the mature dwarf dimmer G4466 with its published WISE W3 and W4 excesses. A continuous detector-response certificate gives a lower apparent dust power of 1.2118 percent of stellar power for any nonnegative spectrum. The value is 1.0638 percent after subtraction of two nominal errors in each band. For a passive 13-Jupiter-mass Roche lobe around a 0.8-solar-mass primary, this requires at least 72.3 percent of isotropic emission outside the lobe. It permits narrow emission features and any temperature mixture. If apparent power can be four times true power, the reduced signals no longer exclude confinement. We give a finite-width nonnegative spectrum that passes that energy test. This limits an extension of the prior smooth-spectrum result; it does not refute that result in its stated family. Limits include the assumed response tables, stellar normalization, published error model, support geometry and directional emission. No new photometry or physical model for the constructed spectrum is claimed. Original code, aggregate results, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Band-energy lower bounds and the required fraction of infrared emission outside one passive planetary Roche lobe. The tested emission direction matters.

citations.reason: Lobe capacity and stellar normalization; we test the energy bound without its smooth-spectrum assumption.
